- Because you’re in France, MMS needs roaming. I saw international data roaming was OFF on your line, which would block MMS while abroad. I’ve just enabled roaming on your line at no cost so your data (and MMS) can work while traveling.

What we need you to do on your phone
Roaming must be ON both on our side (done) and on your device. Please do these in order and stop when MMS starts working. Let me know the first step that fixes it or any error you see.

1) Turn on Data Roaming on the device and test MMS
- Please confirm: are you using Android or iPhone?
- Android: Settings > Network & internet (or Connections) > Mobile network > turn ON Data roaming. Ensure Mobile data is ON. Then turn Wi‑Fi OFF just for this test.
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > turn ON Data Roaming. Ensure Cellular Data is ON. Then turn Wi‑Fi OFF just for this test.
- Optional quick refresh: toggle Airplane mode ON for 10 seconds, then OFF.
- After that, try sending a picture message to a contact (or to yourself).

If MMS still won’t send, continue:

2) Make sure the phone isn’t locked to a slow network mode
- Check your network mode and set it to 4G/5G preferred.
- Android: Settings > Network & internet > Mobile network > Preferred network type > choose 4G/5G (not 2G/3G).
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Voice & Data > choose 4G/5G.

3) Check APN/MMSC settings (common MMS blocker) and reset if needed
- Android: Settings > Network & internet > Mobile network > Access Point Names. Open your active APN and make sure there is an MMSC field filled in. If you’re not sure or it’s blank, reset APN to default (Access Point Names > menu > Reset to default), then reboot the phone.
- iPhone: If MMS still fails, reset network settings: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings (this will reset cellular, Wi‑Fi, and VPN settings). Then reboot.

4) Turn off Wi‑Fi Calling temporarily and test MMS
- Android: Settings > Network & internet > Mobile network > Wi‑Fi Calling > turn OFF.
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular > Wi‑Fi Calling > turn OFF.

5) Ensure the messaging app has required permissions (Android)
- Settings > Apps > Messages (default app) > Permissions > allow SMS and Files/Media (Storage).

Quick confirmation questions
- What phone model and OS (Android or iPhone) are you using?
- After step 1 (Data Roaming ON, Wi‑Fi OFF), what happens when you try to send an MMS? Any specific error?

I’ve enabled roaming on your line already. Once your device’s Data Roaming is ON, MMS should typically start working within a minute or two. If it doesn’t, we’ll proceed with the next steps based on your phone type.

To help you best, could you please provide one of the following to identify your account: your phone number, customer ID, or your full name with date of birth? Also, I will guide you through some quick checks on your phone:

1. Check if Airplane Mode is OFF.
2. Check your SIM status (whether it's active, missing, or locked).
3. If SIM is missing, try removing and reinserting it.
4. Confirm your network mode is set to 4G/5G preferred.
5. Restart your phone.

Once you provide your identifier and the results of these checks, I can look into your line status and assist further.

As soon as I can identify your account, I’ll check your line for suspension (e.g., overdue bill), activation/provisioning issues, or roaming flags and take the appropriate action. I’ll keep you updated at each step.

- Any recent changes (new phone, SIM/eSIM transfer, plan/number change, recent travel).
- Phone make/model (optional).

5. Restart result: After reboot, did service return? If not, do you see “No Signal” in the status bar?

If SIM status shows Locked, please stop entering PIN/PUK and tell me so I can arrange the proper assistance.

If you are traveling outside your home area, please mention it—I can check and enable roaming if needed at no cost.

I’ll immediately look up your line, explain what I find, and take the appropriate action (for example, resolve any billing hold and resume the line). If we resume the line, I’ll ask you to reboot your device to restore service.

messages.content:
To help you best, could you please provide your mobile phone number or other account identifier? Also, while I check on our side, could you please do these quick checks on your phone and share the results?

1. Look at your phone's status bar: Do you see any airplane icon? How many signal bars are there? What network type shows (5G/4G/LTE/3G/2G)? Is there a data icon indicating mobile data is enabled?
2. Check your network status: Is mobile data ON or OFF? What is the signal strength? Is data roaming ON or OFF?
3. Turn off Wi-Fi and run a speed test on your phone. What result do you get (no connection, very poor, poor, fair, good, or excellent)?

If you have time, also check if a VPN is connected or if Data Saver mode is on, and your network mode preference.

Please provide your phone number and the results from these checks so I can assist you further.

Also, what phone make and model are you using, and what OS version is it running (e.g., iPhone 13 iOS 17, Samsung Galaxy S22 Android 14)?

Where are you currently located (city and country), and have you recently traveled outside your usual coverage area?

I have a few questions:
1. Can you place or receive regular phone calls right now?
2. With Wi-Fi turned OFF, can you browse a website using mobile data?
3. Are you currently traveling outside your home country or coverage area?
4. Which messaging app are you using?
5. Do you see any error message when the MMS fails? If yes, what does it say?

From your status bar, please confirm: Airplane mode is OFF, how many signal bars you see, and what network type is shown (5G, LTE, 4G, 3G, or 2G).

If possible, please try these quick checks and let me know the results:
- Turn Wi-Fi OFF and try sending an MMS.
- Ensure Mobile data is ON in Settings > Network/Connections > Mobile data.
- If traveling, turn Data roaming ON in Settings > Mobile network > Data roaming.
- Set Network mode to 4G/5G preferred (not 2G/3G only).
- If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, turn it OFF temporarily and test MMS again.
- Check APN/MMSC in Settings > Mobile network > Access Point Names. Confirm an MMSC/MMS URL exists. If missing or unsure, tap Reset to default, then reboot and test again.
- Check messaging app permissions in Settings > Apps > [Your messaging app] > Permissions. Allow SMS and Photos/Media/Storage (or Files and media).

Please reply with:
- One identifier (phone number, customer ID, or full name + DOB)
- Phone make/model and OS version
- Your current city/country and recent travel status
- Answers to the 5 questions above
- Status bar details (Airplane OFF, signal bars, network type)
- Results of the quick checks (what changed, if anything)

Once I have your identifier, I’ll check your line’s status, data usage, and roaming enablement. If roaming is disabled, I’ll enable it at no cost. If your plan data is exhausted, I can help refuel up to 2GB after confirming the price. I’ll guide any remaining steps until MMS sends successfully.

Your answers will also help confirm if the issue is due to on-device settings like mobile data, network mode, APN/MMSC, Wi-Fi Calling, or app permissions. We’ll make one change at a time and retest.

Please share ONE of the following: the phone number for the affected line, your customer ID, or your full name AND date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD). I can’t run account checks until I have this.

Also, please answer these questions:
1. Are you currently using the device with that phone number?
2. Can you make or receive calls and send plain text SMS right now?
3. With Wi-Fi off and Mobile Data on, can you open a website like example.com?
4. What does the status bar show now? Are there signal bars, network type (5G/4G/3G), and is Airplane Mode off?
5. Are you currently traveling outside your home country or coverage area?
6. Does the messaging app show any specific error when MMS fails?
7. What phone model and OS version are you using (e.g., iPhone 13 iOS 17, Samsung Galaxy S22 Android 14)?

While waiting for your info, please try this quick test and share the result of each step and any error messages:
- Turn Wi-Fi off and ensure Mobile Data is on.
- Send a small photo (under 500 KB) to your own number.
- If it fails, toggle Airplane Mode on for 10 seconds, then off, and try again.
- If still failing, restart the phone and try again.

Additional details that would be helpful:
- Does MMS fail to all contacts or only certain ones?
- Approximate size of the photo you’re sending
- Do you use a VPN? If yes, try with VPN off and share the result
- Is Wi-Fi Calling currently on?

After I identify your account, I will:
- Check line status (Active vs. Suspended).
- Review current cycle data usage versus plan limit; if at limit, we can add data (refuel up to 2 GB) or change plan.
- Verify or enable roaming if you’re outside the home network at no cost.
- Review any recent SIM or plan changes.
- Guide device fixes: confirm Mobile Data is ON; ensure 4G/5G preferred (not 2G/3G only); check/reset APN/MMSC then reboot; temporarily turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF; verify messaging app permissions (Storage and SMS); retest after each step.

Please provide the requested info so we can proceed.

messages.content:
To assist you with your MMS issue, I need to identify your account before I can run line checks such as status, data usage versus your plan limit, and roaming eligibility. Your answers will then help me isolate any on-device causes. We’ll change one thing at a time and retest.

Please provide ONE of the following: (a) phone number with country code, (b) customer ID, or (c) full name AND date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD). I can’t run account checks until I have this.

Also, please answer these questions:
1. Are you currently using the device with that phone number?
2. Can you make or receive calls and send plain text SMS right now?
3. With Wi-Fi off and Mobile Data on, can you open a website like example.com?
4. What does the status bar show now? Are there signal bars, network type (5G/4G/3G), and is Airplane Mode off?
5. Are you currently traveling outside your home country or coverage area?
6. Does the messaging app show any specific error when MMS fails?
7. What phone model and OS version are you using (e.g., iPhone 13 iOS 17, Samsung Galaxy S22 Android 14)?

While waiting for your info, please try this quick test and share the result of each step and any error messages:
- Turn Wi-Fi off and ensure Mobile Data is on.
- Send a small photo (under 500 KB) to your own number.
- If it fails, toggle Airplane Mode on for 10 seconds, then off, and try again.
- If still failing, restart the phone and try again, noting any error messages.

After I identify your account, I will:
- Check your line status (Active vs. Suspended), current cycle data usage versus plan limit, and roaming eligibility.
- If at the data limit, add data (refuel up to 2 GB) or change plan per your preference.
- If outside the home network, enable roaming at no cost if needed.
- Guide device steps: confirm Mobile Data is ON; prefer 4G/5G; check/reset APN/MMSC then reboot; temporarily turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF; verify messaging app permissions (Storage and SMS). Retest after each step.

Please provide the requested info so we can proceed.
